title: How to efficiently detect deleted items via API
body:
I now use added_since/modified_since to update my cache (Thanks for the addition) . This all works, except for detecting deleted items.

Is there a way to detect these without having to query the complete list?

I also asked the question before, but issue got closed: https://github.com/sissbruecker/linkding/issues/899#issuecomment-2901188350. Apologies if you don't want a new issue or if  I am overlooking something.



Version 	1.41.0 (latest)
comments:
There is no other way to detect deleted bookmarks. These get deleted from the database, so there would be no way to query for them. There also isn't an audit trail or similar that keeps a record of what happened.
Any solution in the planning for this?  Even a way to know I need to do a full reload would be sufficient.


No plans

llm_analysis.correct_answer: To efficiently detect deleted items via API, you currently cannot directly query for deleted bookmarks as they are removed from the database without an audit trail. The only way to know about deletions is to perform a full reload of the data.

The user also expressed a need for a solution to detect deletions, but the comments confirm that no such functionality exists.

title: LD_SUPERUSER_NAME and OIDC not compatible
body:
### Version

Running `latest-plus` (1.38.0)

### Background

On a blank install I ran docker as follows, notable: `OIDC` configured and `LD_SUPERUSER_NAME` configured. The LD_SUPERUSER_NAME matches that of my user in my OIDC provider (Authentik). When I attempt to log in once the service is started, I get a server 500 error (user already exists).

I was under the impression that leaving LD_SUPERUSER_PASSWORD blank would work for both OIDC and for Proxy Auth (documentation explicitly calls out proxy auth). Guessing that OIDC follows a different flow and *always* creates a user.

> LD_SUPERUSER_PASSWORD
> 
> Values: String | Default = None
> 
> The password for the initial superuser. When left undefined, the superuser will be created without a usable password, which means the user can not authenticate using credentials / through the login form, and can only be authenticated using proxy authentication (see LD_ENABLE_AUTH_PROXY).

### Workaround

To get to a working state I did the following:

1. from the Django console I deleted myself
2. From the manage.py script I created a new superuser (admin)
3. From the login Page I used OIDC to log in with my creds (the user I deleted in step 1)
4. I logged out of that user and then logged back in with admin
5. From admin's django management page I promoted my OIDC self to superuser

### Expected Behavior

I would expect the superuser env var to work with an OIDC account (especially if no password is set).


Thanks for reading! Let me know if I missed anything!
comments:
Yes, those don't quite fit together. The OIDC implementation looks up users by email, which is a separate field. When you create a user with `LD_SUPERUSER_NAME` it sets a user name, but no email. So the OIDC implementation can not find the user and will create a new one. 

You'd first have to create the super user, then change it's email to what you have in the OIDC provider, and only then enable OIDC. Or create a separate super user, promote your OIDC user to admin and remove the initial super user afterwards.
@sissbruecker ah ok, that makes sense. I had set my `LD_SUPERUSER_NAME` as my email address and since the login name provided by the OIDC provider was the email address I'm guessing that's how they conflicted. I'll write a small blurb for the docs as a PR to at least describe this for the next person that comes along!
Yep, adding something to the docs is probably a good first step. As workflow it make actually make the most sense to not use the superuser env variables and create a user as described here: https://linkding.link/installation/#user-setup. That way you can provide an email address and then OIDC can match that. Still, that needs to be done before logging in the first time with OIDC.
I'm a bit confused, the error I got was that the username already existed, so it should've matched? Or is it maybe that I hadn't populated the email address in the admin user's model and so it tried to create a new user?
> I hadn't populated the email address in the admin user's model and so it tried to create a new user?

It sounds like this one. By default, OIDC uses the email also as username, but since you had already created a user where the username was the same email that failed.

As mentioned above, matching uses the email field, which is separate from the username. So the best approach is probably to first create a superuser manually through the command linked above, with the email field set to what you have in the OIDC provider. Afterwards you can login through OIDC and it should be able to match that superuser.

Make sense, I think I have enough context to make a coherent docs blurb, thanks!

After creating the superuser, you can then enable OIDC, which will allow the system to correctly match the OIDC user with the superuser based on the email.

HI @StephenMottershead,

You can add the line `LD_SINGLEFILE_OPTIONS='--self-extracting-archive=true'` to the `.env.` file.  You will need to make sure that you have the env file option set to have all variables present in it passed to the container.  If you are using docker compose it would be these lines from the [example](https://github.com/sissbruecker/linkding/blob/master/docker-compose.yml):
```yaml
    env_file:
      - .env
```

[https://docs.docker.com/compose/how-tos/environment-variables/set-environment-variables/#use-the-env_file-attribute](https://docs.docker.com/compose/how-tos/environment-variables/set-environment-variables/#use-the-env_file-attribute)

title: web_archive_snapshot_url not showing up in REST API
body:
I enable Internet Archive integration in my Settings and have access to the archived URLs by hovering the timestamp in the Dashboard, but am not sure why `web_archive_snapshot_url` is empty for all my links. The Django admin also doesn't show the snapshot URLs.

Did I overlook anything? Thanks.

(I'm running 1.36.0 on railway)
comments:
Since [1.31.1](https://github.com/sissbruecker/linkding/releases/tag/v1.31.1) the UI will dynamically generate a "fallback" link to the web archive if no specific snapshot URL is stored in the bookmark. But that is not the case for the API currently. I guess it should.

For some background: In general, new snapshots on the IA are only created when you add a single bookmark, either via the UI or the API. It doesn't create snapshots for bookmarks that you have imported though. I removed that functionality as that created a large number of background tasks which then consistently failed due to rate limiting with the web archive API. It also didn't make sense to generate, and then link to, a snapshot from a website in it's current form if the bookmark was added two years ago. So instead it just generates a dynamic link to a snapshot from the time the bookmark was created, and then the IA will usually show you the nearest one. Worst case no snapshot exists but that should be rare.

I guess your issue is with bookmark that were imported then? Otherwise something would be wrong with background tasks, then you could check `background_tasks.log` for errors.
